import smtplib
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart

# ── SMTP Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────
# Update these settings to match your email provider.
SMTP_SERVER = "smtp.example.com"   # e.g., "smtp.gmail.com"
SMTP_PORT = 587                    # 587 for TLS, 465 for SSL
SMTP_USERNAME = "alice@example.com"
SMTP_PASSWORD = "your_password"    # Consider using env vars or app passwords

# ── Email Details ────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM_EMAIL = "alice@example.com"
TO_EMAIL = "bob@example.com"
SUBJECT = "Project Kickoff Meeting – June 10, 2024"

BODY = """\
Hi Bob,

I'd like to invite you to our Project Kickoff Meeting. Here are the details:

  - Date: June 10, 2024
  - Time: 10:00 AM – 11:00 AM (Eastern Time)
  - Location: Conference Room A

We'll be discussing the project goals and deliverables. Looking forward to seeing you there!

Best regards,
Alice
"""

# ── Build & Send ─────────────────────────────────────────────
def send_email():
    msg = MIMEMultipart()
    msg["From"] = FROM_EMAIL
    msg["To"] = TO_EMAIL
    msg["Subject"] = SUBJECT
    msg.attach(MIMEText(BODY, "plain"))

    try:
        with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT) as server:
            server.starttls()
            server.login(SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD)
            server.sendmail(FROM_EMAIL, TO_EMAIL, msg.as_string())
        print("✅ Email sent successfully!")
    except smtplib.SMTPAuthenticationError:
        print("❌ Authentication failed. Check your username/password.")
    except smtplib.SMTPException as e:
        print(f"❌ SMTP error: {e}")
    except ConnectionRefusedError:
        print("❌ Could not connect to the SMTP server. Check server/port settings.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    send_email()
